stories.title: Luna and the Lost Star
stories.description: Luna discovers a tiny lost star and helps it find its way home.

pages.text: Every night, Luna sat by her window and counted the stars. One, two, three... there were always too many to count!
But tonight, something was different. A tiny golden light was hiding behind the flowers in her garden.
Luna hurried outside. There she found a little star glowing softly. "Are you lost?" she asked.
The little star twinkled sadly. Luna looked up and saw one empty spot sparkling in the night sky.
Luna climbed the tallest hill and held the star high above her head. "Try to shine as brightly as you can!"
The star began to glow brighter and brighter until a silver beam reached down from the sky.
Whoosh! The little star floated home. It twinkled three times to thank Luna before joining its friends.
Luna smiled and climbed into bed. From her window, one tiny star seemed to shine just for her. Good night, little star.

stories.takeaway: Helping someone find their way can make both of you shine.

stories.title: Milo and the Tiny Seed
stories.description: Milo learns that even the smallest seed can become something wonderful.

pages.text: Milo loved exploring his grandmother's garden. One morning, he found a tiny brown seed in the soil.
"You're so small," Milo whispered. "I wonder what you could become."
He made a little hole, tucked the seed inside, and covered it gently with soft earth.
Every morning, Milo gave it a little water. Then he waited. And waited. Nothing happened.
One sunny morning, Milo spotted something green. A tiny sprout was pushing through the soil!
Days passed. The sprout grew taller, opened new leaves, and stretched toward the warm sunlight.
At last, a beautiful yellow flower opened. A butterfly landed gently on its petals.
Milo smiled. The tiny seed had taught him something big: wonderful things sometimes need time to grow.

stories.takeaway: Patience and care help living things grow.

stories.title: The Moon Who Couldn't Sleep
stories.description: The Moon searches for peaceful sounds to help her settle down for the night.

pages.text: High above the sleeping world, the Moon was still wide awake.
"How does everyone fall asleep so easily?" she wondered as she watched the quiet houses below.
She listened to the ocean. Whoosh... hush... whoosh... The gentle waves made her feel a little calmer.
Then she heard the wind moving softly through the trees. Rustle... rustle... rustle...
A tiny owl called from the forest, and somewhere far away, gentle rain tapped on a rooftop.
The Moon closed her eyes and listened to all the peaceful sounds together.
Soon her glow became soft and dreamy. "Good night, Earth," she whispered.

stories.takeaway: Quiet sounds and a calm routine can help us relax before sleep.

stories.title: Toby's Ocean Adventure
stories.description: A curious young turtle discovers the colorful world beneath the waves.

pages.text: Toby was a young sea turtle who had always wondered what was beyond his quiet reef.
One bright morning, he took a deep breath and swam farther than he had ever gone before.
He passed a garden of colorful coral where tiny fish zipped between the branches.
A playful dolphin appeared. "Follow me!" she clicked, leading Toby through dancing beams of sunlight.
Suddenly Toby saw a strange bag floating in the water. It did not belong in the ocean.
Toby and his new friends carefully pushed it toward a cleanup boat nearby.
As the Sun began to set, Toby returned to his reef with an amazing story to tell.
The ocean was enormous and full of wonders, Toby realized, but every creature needed help keeping it clean.

stories.takeaway: The ocean is home to many living things, and keeping it clean protects them.

stories.title: Nora's First Trip to Mars
stories.description: Young explorer Nora imagines an unforgettable scientific adventure on Mars.

pages.text: Nora zipped up her spacesuit and looked through the window. A giant red world filled the view. Mars!
The spacecraft landed gently. Nora stepped outside and placed her boots on the dusty ground.
Everything looked rusty red. Nora collected a small rock sample for the science lab.
Her little rover rolled beside her, taking pictures and measuring the ground.
In the distance stood an enormous mountain. Mars has some of the biggest volcanoes in the Solar System.
Before leaving, Nora looked back at her footprints. "Maybe one day explorers really will walk here," she said.
Then Nora opened her eyes. She was back in her bedroom, holding her favorite book about space.
It had been a dream, but Nora knew where real adventures begin: with a question, a book, and a curious mind.

stories.takeaway: Curiosity and learning can take your imagination anywhere.
